<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The provided `pre-commit.sh` script is a Git pre-commit hook designed to automate part of the AUR package maintenance workflow. It checks if the PKGBUILD file is staged, then regenerates the `.SRCINFO` file using `makepkg --printsrcinfo`, which is a standard and safe operation in AUR packaging. It then validates the PKGBUILD using `namcap`, a well-known linter for PKGBUILDs, printing warnings and blocking commits if errors are found.

All commands used (`git diff`, `makepkg --printsrcinfo`, `namcap`, `grep`, `echo`) are standard tools in the Arch Linux packaging environment. The script does not perform any network operations, file exfiltration, code execution from external sources, or system modifications beyond updating `.SRCINFO` and validating the package metadata. The behavior is consistent with typical AUR maintainer helper scripts and poses no security risk.

There is no obfuscated code, suspicious downloads, or unauthorized system access. The script only acts when PKGBUILD is modified and operates solely within the local repository. It enhances package quality rather than introducing risk.
</details>
